plan: This is a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it guarantees you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids, and you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid, not your own. With my value at $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value maximizes my chances of winning while ensuring any profit is truly positive. I will bid exactly $49.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids. Bidding my true value of $44 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (guaranteeing non-negative profit) and lose when it doesn't (avoiding negative profit). Overbidding risks paying more than my value; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a one-shot game with no prior history to exploit, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value adds risk without benefit, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I will bid exactly my value of $22 to maximize expected profit.
